items.question: I got papers from a court. Is this a lawsuit?
items.answer: A summons must name the court in which the action is pending and the parties to the action. It must direct the defendant to file a written pleading in response to the complaint within 30 days after the summons is served. It must also warn that, unless the defendant responds, their default will be entered upon application by the plaintiff, and the plaintiff may then apply to the court for the relief demanded in the complaint, which could result in garnishment of wages, taking of money or property, or other relief.
items.applies_when: A summons issued by a California court.

items.question: What if day 30 falls on a weekend or court holiday?
items.answer: If the last day for performing an act required by law within a specified period is a holiday, the period is extended to and including the next day that is not a holiday. For this purpose a holiday means all day on Saturdays, all holidays specified in Section 135, and, to the extent provided in Section 12b, all days that Section 12b requires to be considered holidays. Section 12b treats a day as a holiday when a city, county, state or public office is closed for the whole of that day, as far as the business of that office is concerned. Section 135 makes every full day designated a holiday by Government Code Section 6700 a judicial holiday, with listed exceptions, and Government Code Section 6700 lists every Sunday as a holiday. Section 135 also makes every Saturday, and the day after Thanksgiving Day, a judicial holiday. This rule applies to all provisions of law requiring an act within a specified period of time.
items.applies_when: Any act required by law to be done within a specified period of time, including a response deadline.

items.question: Does the deadline change if I was not handed the papers?
items.answer: Under Code of Civil Procedure Section 415.20, in effect through December 31, 2026, if a copy of the summons and complaint cannot with reasonable diligence be personally delivered to the person to be served, as specified in Section 416.60, 416.70, 416.80 or 416.90, a summons may be served by leaving a copy at the person's dwelling house, usual place of abode, usual place of business or usual mailing address other than a post office box, in the presence of a competent member of the household or a person apparently in charge, who is at least 18 years of age and who is informed of the contents, and by thereafter mailing a copy by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to that place. Service in this manner is deemed complete on the 10th day after the mailing. The summons directs a response within 30 days after the summons is served. Beginning January 1, 2027, a replacement version of Section 415.20 applies. It provides that a party shows reasonable diligence by attempting personal delivery in good faith on at least three occasions on three different days at three different times; that in an action to collect consumer debt at least one of the attempts shall be made at the dwelling place or usual place of abode if known or reasonably determinable; and that the mailing may be by first-class mail, Priority Mail with tracking, or Certified Mail with return receipt requested. Service is still deemed complete on the 10th day after the mailing.
items.applies_when: Service of a summons by leaving papers with another person and mailing them (substituted service), under Section 415.20(b).
items.harm_flag: Counting from the wrong date can make a person file too late.

items.question: What do I file to respond?
items.answer: An answer to a complaint must contain the general or specific denial of the material allegations the defendant controverts and a statement of any new matter constituting a defense. If the complaint is not verified, or is subject to the economic litigation procedures of Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint. If the complaint is verified, the denial must be made positively or according to the defendant's information and belief. That is also required when the cause of action is a claim assigned to a third party for collection and the complaint is verified, even if the complaint is subject to Article 2. A case is treated as a limited civil case only if all of the conditions in Code of Civil Procedure Section 85 are met, and one of them is that the amount in controversy does not exceed $35,000.
items.applies_when: A response to a collection complaint. What is allowed depends on whether the complaint is verified and whether the claim was assigned for collection.
items.harm_flag: Using a form that is not allowed for this kind of claim may leave the response defective, which risks a default.

items.question: How old is too old for a debt lawsuit?

The period can be extended only under Section 360. The answer must contain a statement of any new matter constituting a defense.

items.question: I made a small payment or signed something on an old debt. Does that restart the clock?
items.answer: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract to take a case out of the operation of the limitations statutes unless it is contained in a writing signed by the party to be charged. Any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged is deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract to stop the running of the time within which an action may be commenced on the note, as each payment is made, and to start the running of a new period. No such payment of itself revives a cause of action once barred. The period for an action on a written instrument is four years.
items.applies_when: Payments or signed writings on a debt that may be near or past the four-year limit.
items.harm_flag: Signing a payment plan or acknowledgment, or paying on a debt near the limit, can weaken the defense that it is too old.

items.question: The 30 days already passed. Is it too late?
items.answer: The court may, upon any terms as may be just, relieve a party from a judgment, dismissal, order or other proceeding taken against the party through the party's mistake, inadvertence, surprise or excusable neglect. The application must be accompanied by a copy of the answer or other pleading proposed to be filed, and must be made within a reasonable time, in no case exceeding six months, after the judgment, dismissal, order or proceeding was taken. This is the version of Code of Civil Procedure Section 473 in effect through December 31, 2026. A replacement version operative January 1, 2027 keeps those subdivisions and adds subdivision (e), which allows a party to bring a motion to vacate a default judgment that is void for lack of proper service at any time after entry of the judgment.

items.question: A collector wrote or called, but there are no court papers. What now?
items.answer: Every debt collector collecting or attempting to collect a consumer debt in California must comply with sections 1692b to 1692j of Title 15 of the United States Code (Civil Code Section 1788.17), but Section 1692g does not apply to the persons that section describes in paragraphs (A) and (B) of 15 U.S.C. 1692a(6) or their principal. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g(a), within five days after the initial communication, a debt collector must, unless the information is in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt, send a written notice with the amount of the debt, the name of the creditor, and statements that the debt will be assumed valid unless the consumer disputes it within thirty days after receipt of the notice, that the collector will obtain verification if the consumer disputes it in writing within that period, and that the collector will give the name and address of the original creditor on written request within that period. If the consumer disputes the debt in writing within the thirty days, the collector must stop collection of the disputed debt until it mails verification (1692g(b)). A consumer's failure to dispute the debt may not be construed by any court as an admission of liability (1692g(c)). A formal pleading in a civil action is not an initial communication (1692g(d)).
items.applies_when: A debt collector's collection of a consumer debt, with or without a lawsuit.
